title: IQM and QAI team up to bring quantum computing to Korean data centers
html:
Finnish quantum computing specialist IQM Quantum Computers has partnered with South Korean quantum-AI infrastructure provider QAI to deploy a 54-qubit quantum computer at its data center in Seoul. The IQM Radiance R3 system is expected to be installed by the end of 2027, marking IQM’s first deployment in a private data center in Asia.

The deal highlights the growing convergence of quantum computing and AI infrastructure in commercial data centers. It also underlines the expanding international footprint of European quantum hardware developers and the business opportunities emerging around hybrid computing.

Bringing quantum computing and AI together

QAI develops data centers that combine GPU-based AI infrastructure with quantum computing resources. Once operational, the IQM system will be made available through QAI’s Quantum-as-a-Service (QaaS) offering, targeting businesses, research institutions and public organizations.

Initial applications will focus on drug discovery, advanced materials and battery development, financial portfolio optimization, logistics and energy infrastructure.

“We are proud to partner with QAI as they bring an IQM Radiance R3 54-qubit quantum computer to their data center in Seoul,” said Sylwia Barthel de Weydenthal, Chief Commercial Officer at IQM Quantum Computers. “This sale marks an important milestone for quantum computing in South Korea. With on-premises access to IQM Radiance, QAI will be able to accelerate research, develop commercial applications for businesses and support sovereign quantum capabilities that keep critical technology and data under national control. We look forward to working closely with QAI to build a thriving quantum ecosystem in Korea and across the Asia-Pacific region.”

Hardware designed for hybrid workloads

The superconducting IQM Radiance R3 is designed for integration into high-performance computing (HPC) environments, reducing latency for hybrid quantum-classical workloads through on-premises deployment.

The 54-qubit system features high-fidelity gates, tunable couplers and a square-lattice architecture that natively supports surface-code error correction. Customers also benefit from pulse-level access and hardware upgrade options.

“By bringing IQM Radiance R3 into our data center in Seoul, we are creating a place where Korean companies and researchers can use GPUs and a quantum computer together to solve real problems,” said Ui-tae Kim, Co-CEO and CTO of QAI. “Together with IQM, we will build an environment where Korea’s industry and research community can work with quantum computing hands-on.”

Expanding IQM’s presence in Asia

The agreement comes as South Korea steps up its investment in quantum technologies. The country aims to achieve the world’s highest quantum computer utilization rate by 2035, while training 10,000 quantum professionals and fostering 2,000 quantum companies.

The QAI order represents IQM’s second quantum computer sale in South Korea, following the installation of an IQM Spark system at Chungbuk National University.

IQM, which opened its Seoul office in June 2025, continues to expand its commercial presence across the Asia-Pacific region, with systems already delivered in South Korea, Taiwan and Japan.

summary: IQM and QAI partner to deploy a 54-qubit quantum computer in Seoul, bringing quantum computing to commercial AI data center infrastructure.
